source.title: Preserving Plasticity in Continual Learning via Dynamical Isometry
source.authors: Andries Rosseau; Robert Müller; Ann Nowé

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own continual-learning training results on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100-related tasks and explicitly distinguishes its setting from single-task training. It tests plasticity and memorization under non-stationarity, rather than the claim's single-task training-error result; its random-label result is a continual-learning aggregate plotted without exact values.
record.gate_note: The paper reports continual CIFAR-10 random-label training accuracy and validation results on permuted/shuffled tasks; these bear on V1's benchmark and training-error outcome, but not on its single-task recipe. The orthogonal initialization and optimizer details are setup, not separate outcome rows. Figure 3's regularization-strength values are a hyperparameter ablation and are not extracted as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses dynamical isometry to develop and evaluate continual-learning methods. Its random-label training results concern MLPs repeatedly adapted across tasks, whereas V1 concerns convolutional networks trained from random initialization. All architectures use orthogonal initialization; no initialization comparison tests V4. The other versions' specified comparisons are also absent.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors argue that approximate dynamical isometry is a tractable surrogate for task-agnostic plasticity under an isotropic input prior, and report that their methods match or outperform continual-learning baselines. Random-label training accuracy measures continued memorization capacity; the paper does not establish V1's convolutional-network convergence claim or experimentally compare initialization choices.
record.recipe_differences: Continual learning across many random-label tasks; compares isometry-promoting methods and plasticity baselines rather than testing the stated single-task training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Orthogonal regularization strength should be tuned: too little does not sufficiently preserve conditioning, while too much can interfere with task optimization (Appendix B.2, Figure 3).

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that isometry-promoting methods outperform plasticity baselines on continual random-label CIFAR-10 memorization by MLPs; exact training-accuracy values are unavailable in the supplied figure text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maintaining approximate isometry during continual training helps MLPs retain the ability to fit newly assigned random labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Continual supervised and reinforcement-learning experiments associate isometry-promoting training with sustained performance, better conditioning and reduced dormant-unit buildup. Initialization is held orthogonal rather than compared.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Promoting isometry throughout training can preserve plasticity under sustained non-stationarity.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The random-label result is shown only as a plot, without exact values or stated uncertainty. It uses continual learning rather than single-task training, and the main text does not give a numerical terminal training accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible result rows identified. Figure 3 varies regularization strength as a hyperparameter ablation; its values are not cataloged as separate benchmark outcome rows.

untested.parts: Training-error convergence of sufficiently large convolutional networks from random initialization on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on size, stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and matched comparisons with identity shortcuts or the specified alternative recipes.
Effects of initialization choice on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss and curvature trajectories relative to an identified stability threshold, recovery above that threshold, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: A different architecture and continual adaptation do not establish a scope limitation on V1. Likewise, benefits from orthogonality regularization during training do not test V4's initialization claim. LayerNorm transformer comparisons do not test batch normalization in V6.

versions.untested_parts: Tests continual CIFAR-10 random-label memorization, not the single-task recipe; no CIFAR-100 random-label result, Adam baseline for the random-label metric, or corrupted-label single-task comparison is reported.

rows.subject: AdamO (ReLU)
rows.size_stated: MLP, depth 4 and size 512 for each hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained across a stream of randomly labeled CIFAR-10 tasks; reports training accuracy.
rows.value: Figure only; training accuracy plotted over 0–16,000 epochs
rows.note: Figure 1 identifies the random-label memorization condition and reports training accuracy as the measure, but supplies no numerical values. The text says methods consistently outperform competing approaches; the plot includes AdamO (ReLU), NS (ReLU), NaP, SN Reg, ReDo, Baseline, and others. It does not state the plotted terminal value in prose.
rows.check: R1 measures continual random-label memorization by an MLP using AdamO, not V1's convolutional-network training from random initialization. It compares the study's own method with plasticity baselines. The supplied figure text contains axes and legends but no readable curve values, so the assigned partial state is unsupported. The caption specifies 256 epochs/task across 200 tasks, while the extracted axis ends at 16,000; the displayed coverage cannot be resolved from this text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
